target_customer: Underbanked and self-employed consumers in Mexico needing small short-term loans
problem: Many Mexicans lack access to formal credit; Baubap lends small amounts via app using alternative data.
business_model: Consumer microlending (interest and fees), funded by debt facilities

founders.name: Luis Villarreal
founders.background_notes: Met Salcedo in 2016 at a media company per Crunchbase News.

technical_complexity.rationale: Automated credit scoring on alternative data for first-time borrowers, plus a fully digital loan flow and collections; standard fintech engineering with a hard underwriting problem.

defensibility.rationale: Repayment data on millions of thin-file borrowers and a SOFOM licence help, but digital lenders such as Kueski and Tala sell similar short-term loans.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent copy or purchase found; in 2026 BBVA's venture debt arm Spark lent to Baubap rather than competing.

market_need_then: Crunchbase News (Mar 2021) reports loan approval around 25%, average loan about 50 pesos, 40% self-employed borrowers, expecting 220,000+ loans in 2021, indicating unmet small-credit demand.

brand_strength.rationale: Over two million borrowers and a recognisable invented name, but no sourced press about the brand, mascot or community; rating rests on scale only.

outcome_analysis: Baubap grew from a 2018 Mexican microloan app to over two million borrowers and over half a million active loans a month by 2024, funded mainly by debt: $20M in 2022, $120M in 2024 and about $23M from BBVA Spark and SixPoint in 2026. Growth looks driven by unmet demand for very small loans from unbanked borrowers, though loans carry very high rates and equity funding beyond a $3M seed is not public.
notes: Directory Active, consistent. Seed lead: Crunchbase News says Grupo Alfin, while a search summary named Grupo Grameen; Alfin kept. Seed predates YC S21 by under 4 months. $120M debt dated 2024-02-28 by LatamList (crowdfundinsider says 2024-03; Feb used). $20M (2022-11-25, Contxto, Park Cities) now sourced from a fetched article with a second mention in search results. 2026-06 facility is MX$400M (about $23M, 48 months per BBVA via search summary), tranche split senior BBVA Spark and mezzanine SixPoint. Equity after the seed may be missing, so coverage partial. Contxto says founded 2019 versus 2018 elsewhere; 2018 used. Regulatory note: operates as a SOFOM; one 2026 source quotes very high APRs (CAT 1,355%), a consumer-harm risk. Competitors dated 2021 were not found; Kueski, Tala, Moneyman, DiDi Prestamos and Creditas appear only in 2025-26 sources, so the list is empty. Name origin not found.
